config.title: line-clamp

intro.title: line-clamp
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll learn how to use the CSS line-clamp property to limit text to a specific number of lines. You'll create a card component with a title and description, then apply line-clamp to truncate the description after three lines with an ellipsis. The core concept involves controlling text overflow and creating clean, readable layouts. You'll work with CSS properties like display, -webkit-line-clamp, and text-overflow to achieve this effect. This technique is essential for creating consistent, space-efficient designs in modern web interfaces.
intro.usecase: The line-clamp property is essential for controlling text overflow in modern web interfaces. Developers use it to create clean, consistent layouts in product cards, article previews, and dashboard tables where space is limited. For example, e-commerce sites apply line-clamp to truncate long product descriptions, while news apps use it to limit article summaries in feed views. This technique ensures UI elements remain visually balanced and prevents text from breaking the design.

objectives: Apply the line-clamp property to limit text to a specific number of lines
Configure line-clamp with different numeric values to control text truncation
Integrate line-clamp with overflow and display properties for proper rendering
Manipulate text content to observe line-clamp behavior changes
Initialize CSS custom properties to dynamically control line-clamp values
Construct responsive designs using line-clamp with media queries
Implement fallback styles for browsers that don't support line-clamp

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure for testing line-clamp
steps.instruction: Create a div element with a class of 'text-container' containing a paragraph with several lines of text
steps.hint: Start with a div element and give it a class attribute. Inside the div, add a paragraph element with enough text content to create multiple lines.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example: basic container with text */

This is a paragraph with multiple lines of text that will wrap and create a block of content for styling purposes.
steps.seedCode: This is a paragraph with multiple lines of text that will wrap and create a block of content for styling purposes. Add more text here to ensure it spans several lines when rendered in the browser.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a basic HTML structure with a div container and a paragraph containing multi-line text, ready to be styled with CSS line-clamp.
successCriteria: A div element with class 'text-container' exists and contains a paragraph element with sufficient text to create multiple lines.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the div with class 'text-container' and a paragraph with enough text inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match what's needed. Create a div with class 'text-container' containing a paragraph with multi-line text.

steps.title: Add basic styling to the text container
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the .text-container class that sets width to 300px, padding to 20px, a 2px solid gray border, and font-size to 16px.
steps.hint: Create a CSS selector for .text-container and define the properties inside curly braces.
steps.seedCode:
This is a paragraph with multiple lines of text that will wrap and create a block of content for styling purposes. Add more text here to ensure it spans several lines when rendered in the browser.

/* Add your CSS rule here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The text container will have a fixed width, padding, border, and readable font size, making it a visible block for further styling.
successCriteria: The .text-container selector has width: 300px, padding: 20px, border: 2px solid gray, and font-size: 16px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but check if all required properties (width, padding, border, font-size) are present with the specified values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule for .text-container is missing or incomplete. Ensure you define all four properties with the correct values.

steps.title: Introduce the overflow property
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property overflow: hidden to the .text-container rule to hide any content that extends beyond the container's boundaries.
steps.hint: The overflow property controls what happens when content overflows its container. Use 'hidden' to clip the overflow.
steps.seedCode:
This is a paragraph with multiple lines of text that will wrap and create a block of content for styling purposes. Add more text here to ensure it spans several lines when rendered in the browser.

.text-container { /* Add overflow: hidden here */ }
steps.expectedOutcome: The .text-container rule now includes overflow: hidden, which will clip any text that extends beyond the container.
successCriteria: The CSS rule for .text-container includes the property overflow: hidden.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added overflow: hidden to the .text-container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .text-container rule should include overflow: hidden to control content overflow.

steps.title: Apply display: -webkit-box to enable line-clamp
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property display: -webkit-box to the .text-container selector in your stylesheet.
steps.hint: This property enables the WebKit box model, which is required for the line-clamp functionality to work.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .text-container will have display: -webkit-box applied, setting up the foundation for line-clamp.
successCriteria: The .text-container selector includes display: -webkit-box in its CSS rules.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added display: -webkit-box to the .text-container selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The display: -webkit-box property is missing. Add it to the .text-container selector to enable line-clamp.

steps.title: Set the -webkit-box-orient property
steps.instruction: Add the -webkit-box-orient property with the value 'vertical' to the .text-container selector.
steps.hint: This property tells the browser to arrange the text content vertically within the container, which is necessary for line-clamp to work correctly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .text-container selector now includes the -webkit-box-orient: vertical property, configuring the text flow direction for line-clamp.
successCriteria: The CSS rule for .text-container includes -webkit-box-orient: vertical.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added -webkit-box-orient: vertical to the .text-container selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding -webkit-box-orient: vertical to the .text-container selector. Please add this property.

steps.title: Implement -webkit-line-clamp property
steps.instruction: Add the -webkit-line-clamp property to the .text-container selector and set it to 3 to limit the visible text to three lines.
steps.hint: The -webkit-line-clamp property works with display: -webkit-box and -webkit-box-orient: vertical to control how many lines of text are shown before truncation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .text-container selector now includes -webkit-line-clamp: 3; to restrict text display to three lines.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added -webkit-line-clamp: 3; to the .text-container selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The -webkit-line-clamp property is missing or incorrect. Add -webkit-line-clamp: 3; to the .text-container selector.

steps.title: Test different line-clamp values
steps.instruction: Change the -webkit-line-clamp value from 3 to 2 in your CSS rule.
steps.hint: Look for the comment where -webkit-line-clamp should be added and replace it with the property set to 2.
steps.expectedOutcome: The text will now be limited to a maximum of 2 lines instead of 3.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've changed the -webkit-line-clamp value to 2.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. Check that you've changed the -webkit-line-clamp value to 2 in the CSS rule.

steps.title: Add text overflow ellipsis
steps.instruction: Add the text-overflow: ellipsis property to the .text-container rule to show an ellipsis (...) when text is truncated.
steps.hint: The text-overflow property works with overflow: hidden to display an ellipsis for clipped text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .text-container rule now includes text-overflow: ellipsis to visually indicate truncated text with an ellipsis.
successCriteria: The .text-container selector includes the text-overflow: ellipsis property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added text-overflow: ellipsis inside the .text-container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The text-overflow property is missing or incorrect. Add text-overflow: ellipsis to the .text-container rule.

steps.title: Create multiple text containers with different line limits
steps.instruction: Add two new CSS rules: one for a class named '.text-container-1' with '-webkit-line-clamp: 1', and another for '.text-container-4' with '-webkit-line-clamp: 4'. Both should include all the other line-clamp properties from the existing .text-container rule.
steps.hint: Copy the existing .text-container rule twice, change the class names, and modify the -webkit-line-clamp values as specified.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have three CSS rules with different line-clamp values (1, 3, and 4) ready to apply to different HTML elements.
successCriteria: Two new CSS rules exist: .text-container-1 with -webkit-line-clamp: 1 and .text-container-4 with -webkit-line-clamp: 4, both containing all required line-clamp properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both new rules include all the necessary properties: overflow: hidden, display: -webkit-box, -webkit-box-orient: vertical, and the correct -webkit-line-clamp value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rules aren't quite right. Remember to create two new class rules with different -webkit-line-clamp values (1 and 4) and include all the line-clamp properties from the existing .text-container rule.

steps.title: Review and consolidate the complete line-clamp implementation
steps.instruction: Add the missing text-overflow: ellipsis; property to the .text-container rule to complete the line-clamp implementation.
steps.hint: Look for the comment in the .text-container rule that indicates where to add the text-overflow property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .text-container rule will have all four required properties for proper line-clamp functionality with ellipsis truncation.
successCriteria: The .text-container rule includes text-overflow: ellipsis; property alongside overflow, display, -webkit-box-orient, and -webkit-line-clamp.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added text-overflow: ellipsis; to the .text-container rule where the comment indicates.
steps.feedbackWrong: The line-clamp implementation is incomplete. Add text-overflow: ellipsis; to the .text-container rule to show ellipsis when text is truncated.
